24953.description:
Lead strategy & corporate services for essential PNG operations.
Drive cultural change and develop a high-performing team.
Build a lasting legacy and shape the organisation's future.
An exciting opportunity exists for a seasoned corporate services professional to join a dynamic organisation focused on delivering 
essential services and infrastructure
 to the people of Papua New Guinea. 
Our client is an organisation committed to 
integrity, accountability, and excellence
, fostering a culture where every employee is valued, and their contributions are essential to the collective success of the company. 
They believe in providing a supportive environment that promotes 
professional growth and skill development
, ensuring a safe, ethical, and engaging workplace for all. Their core operations involve the development, management, and provision of critical infrastructure and services.
 
 
The Role: General Manager Corporate Services  
 
The client is seeking a high-calibre 
General Manager Corporate Services
 to provide strong leadership and management to the Corporate Services department, ensuring all corporate services are delivered in a timely, efficient manner, and to a high quality, enabling effective delivery of their core services. 
Reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer, the successful candidate will be based in Port Moresby on a full-time basis. This role is vital for maximising the organisations ability to achieve strategic goals by enabling a professional, achievement-focused organisation and promoting a strong internal service culture.
 
 
Key Responsibilities   
 The General Manager Corporate Services will be accountable for a broad range of functions, including:
 
 
Strategic Leadership and Planning:
 Assisting the CEO with the ongoing development, implementation, and monitoring of the company's strategic plan as it relates to Corporate Services, and establishing departmental targets that support company goals.  
 
Human Resources Oversight:
 Managing the HR team, overseeing the function to ensure the company attracts, develops, and retains highly engaged staff. This includes advising the CEO and Executive Management Team on HR matters, recommending policies, and managing staff communication and culture to align with strategic goals.      
 
ICT and Business Systems:
 Ensuring cost-effective, best practice, and sustainable ICT capability, including overseeing data security, technology upgrades, and providing strategic advice on business systems.     
 
Safety, Security, and Risk:
 Overseeing the delivery of effective risk management strategies to ensure the safety and security of staff and assets, and managing security personnel and operations.     
 
Financial and Compliance:
 Maintaining responsibility and accountability for Corporate Services expenditure and ensuring compliance with all company financial and procurement policies and procedures.     
 
Administration:
 Maintaining office efficiency, planning and implementing office systems, overseeing corporate records and asset registries, and managing vendor and office lease contracts.     
 
Performance Management and Culture:
 Implementing and maintaining a robust performance management system, coaching and supporting the Corporate Services management team, and providing a leadership role in driving the desired organisational culture.  
 
 
Key Requirements   
 To be considered for this crucial role, you must possess:
 
 
Education:
 A Bachelor's Degree in HR, Business Management or Administration, Public Administration, or a relevant field.     
 
Experience:
 At least 
5-10 years of leadership and management experience
 in a similar role.     
 
Proven Track Record:
 Demonstrated success in preparing corporate strategy, finance management that supports core business and culture, and managing organisational risk and compliance.     
 
Technical Skills:
 Competency and hands-on experience in trending HR/Payroll, Safety, and IT software, along with good MS Skills.    
 
Personal Attributes:
 Excellent communication (written, verbal, and oral) and active listening skills, with the ability to build effective working relationships and address conflicts constructively. The ideal candidate is a self-reliant, motivated, and resilient leader who is driven to achieve goals, proactive, and demonstrates great attention to detail. 
 
 If you are a driven leader with a proven track record in corporate services and a passion for supporting essential services, we encourage you to apply. 
Please submit your CV and cover letter outlining your experience against the key requirements.
Peopleconnexion PNG: Recruitment, Training, Payroll & HR Services
 
 
Your legacy is our business
www.peopleconnexion.com/png






Apply

24156.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Joining our Operational Services maintenance team, this role is responsible for monitoring the overall mine site power supply and distribution network including all Permanent Power Station generators and associated controls. In addition, you will maintain of all High Voltage electrical supply equipment and oversee the maintenance of all Permanent Power Station generators and associated controls.


Training of HV Electrical Technicians to effectively monitor and maintain the electrical systems on the mine site, with reference to the electrical components.


Key Accountabilities




Monitor Network supply and communicate with Mining and Processing Operations regarding power supply matters, including changeover of power supplies from PPS to PPL or vice versa, if required.


Prepare High Voltage Switching sheets, understand and follow Safe Operating Procedures related to High Voltage equipment.


Monitor Generators when they are operational and supplying Power to site.


Work with contractors and mechanical staff to maintain Generators so they are in good working order.


Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.


Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.


Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.


Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.


Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.


Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment and machines.


Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.


Be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.


Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.


Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.


Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy




About You 


To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a 
NATTB Trade Certificate
 as well a current 
electrical license
. You will also need to demonstrate experience in the installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control centres, LVHV transfers, motor starters and controls; and in the maintenance of equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.




Experience in High Voltage switching and Power Station Operation and Maintenance


A certified electrician with 5 years’ work experience in a mining environment.


Must be a Tradesman with PPL certification.


Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.


Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.


Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the


equipment availability is high.


Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.


Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.




Life at K92  


K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.


In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP 






Apply

25111.description:
Mine Engineer
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.
We are currently seeking a
Mine Engineer
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 15/13 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins or Tabar group of Islands.
(Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Senior Mine Engineer, the Mine Engineer, is responsible for the preparation of the short term (< 3 Mths) mine engineering and mine planning activities, ensuring Simberi Operations adheres to the site business plans and strategy to realise maximum return for the asset. The role will also provide technical and processional leadership and support to the Simberi Operations, which will be consistent with the Company’s Vision, Values and Policies.
The opportunity
Technical Accountabilities
Mine Planning
Work with the technical services and mining teams to develop short to medium term schedules and forecasts in line with company targets and objectives.
Support the mining operations team to achieve production targets by providing technical support in terms of mine design and planning.
Assist the senior mining engineer in the development and implementation of mine planning and scheduling system, processes, and procedures.
Assist the senior mining engineer with their efforts to ensure that the mine planning team provides a consistently high level of support to mining operations at Simberi.
Coordinate and consult with the mining department and the tech services team to ensure that all the daily mining and planning activities are conducted in a manner which allows safe and efficient mining operations.
Assist with tracking, reporting and analysis of daily, weekly, and monthly mining related production data.
Drill and Blast
Assist with the planning and design of blast holes, tie ups and charging plans as required and provide technical support to the Drill & Blast Team.
Assist with the planning and scheduling of drill and blast operations in line with the short term mine plan and integrate this work with other planning and operational areas.
With the support of the planning team, actively engage with the production team to communicate designs and plans to ensure that the drill & blast processes are optimised.
People Accountabilities
Coordinate resources for the effective delivery of all production planning requirements
Coach, mentor and train the mine engineering team to ensure tasks are consistently completed to a high standard to ensure that mining operations can meet targets and operate efficiently and effectively.
Provide direction and leadership for mining engineers, graduate engineers and others
Are you ready to come and build our future together?
We need the right people. Our vision is to build a high performing mine technical services team to cover all technical mining engineering activities from short term to strategic mine planning, with all work completed on site and minimal reliance on external consultants.
We are looking for people who are highly motivated, have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact.  Additionally, we are looking for people who see a challenge as an opportunity for personal growth and development and value working in a team towards a common goal.
We would love to hear from you if you have:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara Values
Ability to produce a PNG National Police Clearance (valid within the last 3 months) for site access purposes
Current unencumbered Papua New Guinea’s ‘C’ Class Driver’s Licence
A degree qualification in mining engineering or related discipline
At least three (3) years’ experience in the mining industry, with appropriate experience in Open Pit mining.
Experienced user of mine design, drill and blast and scheduling software
High level of enthusiasm for the work with high performance goals for self and team
Effective multitasking skills and the ability to work under pressure
Excellent analytical and teamwork skills
Good written and verbal communication skills as well as good organizational and administrative skills.
Desirable
Experience using Deswik software highly desirable.
A Shot Firers permit and Explosive handling certification.
Knowledge of the PNG Mine Safety Act and Regulations
Ability to lead a group of technical professionals
For further information on the
Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/TYD98
Closing date: Friday, 21
st
of November 2025 at close of business.
Please submit your Applications, CVs, and Supporting documents (all merged in one PDF document
At Simberi Gold Company Limited, we’re committed to finding the best fit for every role. We are a diverse and inclusive workplace, welcoming diversity in all its forms. All qualified applicants will be given equal consideration, regardless of their race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.

VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT 


 


Position: 
Logistics and Admin Officer


Full-Time, Fixed-Term position until 30 Sept 2026, with possible extension


 


Location: 
MAG PNG Office, Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea with travel throughout PNG, especially to MAG project locations. 


 


Salary:
 The starting monthly salary for this position is 2960 PGK


 


About MAG:


 


MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.


 


About the role:


 


MAG PNG is currently seeking to recruit a Logistics and Admin Officer to join the team in our Port Moresby office and contribute to our work on reducing armed violence in PNG. The Logistics and Admin Officer is responsible for ensuring that all logistics administrative processes are completed efficiently, including maintaining and controlling equipment, maintaining logistics paperwork and record systems in compliance with Logistics Standard Operating Procedures. Additionally, this role will have some general office administrative responsibilities.


 


Responsibilities include: 


 


Procurement 




Manage day-to-day procurement activities, ensuring compliance with MAG Logistics procedures, policies, and donor requirements.


Assist in preparing and issuing Requests for Quotations (RFQ) and Purchase Orders (PO). Collect supplier quotes in line with MAG procurement policies.


Maintain accurate procurement records and ensure proper documentation and filing.


Liaise with suppliers and service providers to ensure timely and accurate completion of orders.


Cultivate effective supplier relationships to achieve the best possible price, quality, service, and terms for MAG.


Compile and manage a supplier database and establish preferred suppliers.


Regularly review price comparisons and monitor material/item costs.


Prepare and distribute weekly procurement reports to the Security and Access Manager and Country Director (CD), addressing any procurement-related issues.




 


Asset and Inventory Management




Record all purchases of Capital and Non-Capital Assets, ensuring they are asset tagged


Maintain an up-to-date Asset Register and submit a monthly copy to the Security and Access Manager and CD.


Update the Assets Database to ensure effective asset tracking, including adding newly procured equipment and asset encoding.


Liaise with the Security and Access Manager and CD regarding asset-related matters.


Ensure that all staff return all MAG assets upon departure from the programme.


Perform other tasks assigned by the line manager, which may include aspects of asset management.


Support inventory management of stocks and tool handover/takeover processes.


Monitor product quality, expiry dates, and ensure cleanliness and organization of storage areas.


Issue and record store items accurately; maintain organized and compliant stock documentation.




 


Distribution:




Collect and dispatch new equipment/supplies as required.


Verify goods for quality, quantity, and compliance with specifications.


Organize transportation of equipment/supplies to areas of operation.


Ensure accurate recording of incoming supplies/equipment on Goods Received Notes.




Office Administration: 




Establish and maintain proper and up-to-date filing systems (paper and electronic) for efficient organization of office records, files, and documents.


Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence, emails, and calls.


Schedule and coordinate meetings, appointments, and travel arrangements in coordination with the Security & Access Manager.


Manage office supplies and equipment inventory, and order as needed.


Assist in trip planning and coordination.


Assist in managing travel and immigration matters for MAG staff in the country and visiting staff, including visas, permits, flight reservations, hotel bookings, and transport arrangements.




 


General Responsibilities:




Work within the framework of MAG’s core values.


Maintain professional conduct in line with MAG’s core values as actions represent MAG.


Contribute to other fundraising initiatives where appropriate.


Participate in meetings as relevant.


Understand and uphold the standards outlined in MAG’s Safeguarding Framework, acting with due care and attention to safeguard the wellbeing of anyone that comes into contact with MAG’s work and reporting concerns if they do arise.


Undertake and apply learning from appropriate training and development programs.


Undertake any other duties as may be required.




 


About you:


 


The successful candidate will:


Essential Experience  




Demonstrated experience in procurement and logistics


Previous administration experience




Essential Skills and Knowledge 




Strong negotiation skills


Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to prioritise work and meet deadlines


Proficiency in databases and Microsoft Office Suite


Language requirements – Fluent in written/spoken English




Essential Aptitude 




Ability to work calmly under pressure


Ability to work with minimal supervision


Detail-oriented with strong problem-solving skills


Ability to demonstrate initiative, be proactive and offer a solution-oriented approach.


Determined and committed to high quality standards


Understanding of NGOs and a commitment to MAG’s humanitarian mandate




Desirable




NGO experience




 


Please note that as part of MAG's commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed.


 


MAG is committed to the principles of diversity, equality and inclusion. If you think you would be suited to one of our roles we would welcome your application regardless of your background. We strive to provide an inclusive and supportive working environment where all employees feel respected and supported in fulfilling their potential.


 


 


HOW TO APPLY


Application is by submission of a CV and covering letter in English. The covering letter stating why She / He is interested in the job and why you think you would be a good candidate.


 


This should be sent by email to

As part of MAG’s commitment to safeguarding, this post is subject to background checks before an offer of employment is confirmed.

24942.description:
PNG's pioneering leader in logistics and property.
Develops staff; invests in PNG's health & education.
Offers stable, rewarding careers with long-term growth.
The Opportunity
 
 
 
 This organization is known as a pioneering icon and diversified leader in Papua New Guinea's development, having grown from a single-vessel trading operation into one of the country's largest private employers by diversifying across shipping, transport, property, and hospitality.
 
 This is a perfect opportunity if you are a detail-oriented, proactive professional with a strong background in data analysis and reporting within the logistics, transport, or shipping industry. This role is ideal for those looking to elevate their career by automating reporting tasks, streamlining data processes, and directly impacting business strategy to improve operational efficiency and customer service delivery.
 
 
 
 
The Role
 
 
 
 Your core mission is to drive the organization's success by transforming raw logistics and shipping data into actionable insights that enhance operational efficiency, optimize fleet performance, and drive strategic decision-making. You will be directly responsible for developing and maintaining key reports and dashboards using tools like Power BI and Azure, ensuring data integrity and compliance with regulatory standards, and collaborating with operational and finance teams to streamline reporting processes and contribute to informed management decisions.
 
 
Main duties include:
 
 
Report Development and Maintenance: Create and maintain reports and dashboards, specifically using tools like Power BI and Azure, including the preparation of monthly Balanced Scorecards.
 
Data Collection and Validation: Compile and verify data from logistics systems and external sources (like Excel and delivery schedules) to ensure accuracy.
 
Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with the four operating companies (OpCos) and finance teams to understand their reporting needs and deliver customised solutions.
 
Process Optimisation: Identify and implement solutions to automate routine reporting tasks (e.g., daily updates) and streamline data processes to improve responsiveness.
 
Documentation and Training: Create a repository of data sources, capture operational details (Standard Operating Procedures), and train end-users on reporting functions and data integrity.
 
Data Integrity and Security: Uphold the accuracy and confidentiality of data, ensuring compliance with both company policies and Papua New Guinea's regulatory standards.
 
 
Qualification and Experience:
 
 
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Accounting or Finance.
 
2-4 years of experience in MIS, reporting, or data analysis, ideally within the logistics, transport, or shipping industry.
 
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong experience with reporting tools like Power BI or similar platforms. Familiarity with logistics software (Cargowise, TM Master, Cadi) or SQL is a strong advantage.
 
 If this role is the next step in your exciting career, please register your interest by clicking APPLY NOW and submitting your most recent CV in Microsoft Word format.
 Peopleconnexion PNG: Recruitment, Training, Payroll & HR Services
 Your legacy is our business
 
www.peopleconnexion.com/png

25187.description:
Drug Resistant Tuberculosis in PNG and the Western Province TB program.
PNG is one of only 14 countries classified by the WHO as having the triple high burden of TB, MDR-TB, and TB-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Three hotspot regions have been identified in the country including the Gulf, National Capita District (NCD), and Western Province. In Western province, the problem has been further compounded by high levels of drug-resistant TB, with evidence of primary (person to person) transmission of resistant strains, particularly in Daru of South Fly District.
The Western Province TB program, led by the WPHA, with support from partners has led to commendable success, with an increasing recognition of Daru as a ‘Centre of excellence’ in the programmatic management of DR TB with outstanding treatment outcomes for patients.
We are seeking qualified and experienced professionals for the following position(s):
Position:
Operations Coordinator
Classification:
Full-time, contract
Location:
Daru, Western Province (WP)
Role Purpose
The purpose of the operations Coordinator role is to oversee the day-to-day management of the Daru based logistics support team, lead WP project asset management and to provide support to the WP team. The role will report directly to the Team Leader – Operations and be part of an experienced team of managers, clinicians and public health professionals based in Daru, Port Moresby and Melbourne , providing inputs in WP. The role works to ensure efficient operation of the Burnet Daru office and the timely and efficient delivery of support services to the team.
The Operations Coordinator will be responsible for assisting the Team Leader – Operations to ensure the efficient management and implementation of all operational, logistical, financial, and administrative tasks in line with Burnet Institute PNG policies and practice.
Reporting and supervision:
The Operations Coordinator position will be supervised by and report directly to the Team Leader - Operations, based in Daru. This position has 6 direct reports, Logistics Coordinator, Logistics Officer, two Drivers and two office attendants. During the absences of the Team Leader – Operations the Operations Coordinator is expected to act in the role.
Core Responsibilities
1.
Logistics
Coordinates the day-to-day logistics of the operations of the WP teams including decentralized sites and staff to support project activities. This includes publishing a weekly logistics support plan
Manage fleet maintenance, vehicle spot checks, and driver compliance.
Support the design and implementation of a fleet logbook system, train staff and ensure compliance?
Leadership and supervision of the logistics team
2.
Procurement, Event and Activity Planning
Manage office supplies and stationery and ensure the proper maintenance of office equipment.
Conduct monthly checks on stocks and supplies and coordinate ordering of supplies
Coordinate operational and administrative support for the planning, coordination and implementation of project visits, activities, workshops and other trainings and events adhering to Burnet policies and procedures.
3.
Office Health, Safety and Security
Lead and supervise office attendants to ensure a hygienic and safe workplace is provided in both Daru offices.
Conduct fire drills and ensure safety equipment is in place
Support the Team Leaders Operations, in collaboration with senior managers, to ensure security risks for the team’s operations are identified early and well managed.
Take the lead on and support staff with incident reporting in a timely manner
4.
Finance and asset management
TechOne responsibilities

601 Engineering Limited is an engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) company based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, specializing in the energy sector, particularly fuel storage, bulk aviation facilities, and oil and gas projects. We also provide engineering consulting services for mechanical projects and offer renovation services for commercial and government buildings.
Position Overview:
We are seeking a skilled and experienced
Project Manager
to oversee our OTE Aviation Project. The successful candidate will be responsible for the overall supervision and coordination of site activities, ensuring successful project execution while adhering to safety, quality, and regulatory standards.
Key Responsibilities:
Overall Site Supervision & Coordination:
Act as the primary on-site contact for daily construction activities across multiple disciplines (civil, structural, mechanical, piping, instrumentation, electrical). Ensure alignment of work with project scope and specifications.
Discipline Integration & Multi-Trade Management:
Manage the integration of various trades, ensuring adherence to schedules and quality standards. Provide technical oversight to crews.
Quality Assurance / Control:
Inspect work in progress to verify compliance with project specifications and quality standards. Track non-conformances and facilitate corrective actions.
Health, Safety, Environment & Regulatory Compliance:
Implement safe work practices and ensure compliance with safety regulations. Prepare and enforce Job Safety Analyses (JSA) for high-risk tasks.
Schedule, Cost & Progress Monitoring:
Track daily progress and report on status, identifying risks and proposing mitigation actions.
Resource & Logistics Management:
Supervise site workforce and manage materials and equipment logistics effectively.
Communication & Stakeholder Engagement:
Serve as a communication link between site teams, contractors, clients, and internal functions. Conduct regular site meetings to ensure alignment.
Commissioning, Turnover & Close-Out:
Supervise the handover of constructed scope and support final inspections and close-out reports.
Specific Considerations for a Fuel Loading Facility:
Ensure compliance with hazardous area regulations and oversee construction of containment systems.
Coordinate mechanical piping and instrumentation works, ensuring environmental controls are in place.
Support commissioning activities, ensuring alignment with safety and operational readiness.
Typical Skills & Qualifications:
Proven experience in supervising multi-discipline construction projects, preferably in industrial, energy, or fuel/storage environments.
Strong understanding of civil, structural, mechanical, piping, and electrical/instrumentation scopes.
Excellent leadership, communication, and coordination skills.
Ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications.
Strong organizational and planning abilities.
Solid safety mindset with knowledge of WHS/OSHA/NEBOSH standards.
Relevant certifications and a degree/diploma in Construction Management, Engineering, or related field are preferred.

Interfaces with: Site Engineers, QA/QC team, HSE team, Procurement/Logistics team, and Subcontractor Supervisors.

.

Islands Petroleum is an independently owned fuel and lubes distributor, and the exclusive distributor for Mobil lubricants in Papua New Guinea. With the head office based in Kokopo, Islands Petroleum also operates bulk fuel depots in Rabaul, Kimbe, Konebada, Kavieng, Alotau, Popondetta/ Orobay and Mt. Hagen as well as lubes and fuel distribution warehouses in Lae, Port Moresby, and Madang.
We are currently seeking to hire an experienced Depot Manager for our Mt. Hagen Depot operations in Western Highlands Province.
The Role & Responsibilities
Reporting to the Regional Manager, the Depot Manager will be responsible for directing, coordinating, and managing the day-to-day operations of our Depot including sales and delivery of fuel and lubricant products and ensure efficient customer service delivery in an environmentally responsible and safe manner.
Other responsibilities include:
Manage stock on site and stock orders.
Responsible for the sales and inventory management of the Depot in ensuring that sales and inventory monitored and reconciled reflecting same periodically. Observes adequate replenishment cycles to ensure optimum stock levels for all products.
Responsible for the efficiency and cost-effectiveness of all aspects of the GENCO and preventive maintenance programs in accordance with the maintenance plans and schedules.
Promotes occupational health and safety standards and programs targeting zero environmental damage, work-related injuries, and illnesses. Establishes a culture of safety awareness underpinned by an understanding of the principles of duty of care throughout the company’s workforce.
Reviews operating gain and loss reports submitted by the Depot Stock Clerk.
Responsible for the management of all company assets and ensuring that the assets are maintained at operational standards.
Reviews projections for capital and operating expenditure and regularly monitors performance against budgeted financial targets to minimize costs without adversely impacting efficiencies.
Examines technical trends as they affect the depot’s maintenance activities and proactively implements programs to minimize risks and optimize opportunities, with respect to efficiencies in operation and maintenance procedures.
Ensures that employees in the company are highly motivated, competent, and well trained and effective systems are in place to provide feedback on performance levels and encourage a high-performance work culture.
Ensure that all depot reports are done and submitted in a timely manner
Supervises and mentors all employees. Manages workforce performance, be aware of various depots or customer issues and be ready to proactively address them.
Administers terminal depot programs and ensures that all employees have met requirements
Candidates Requirements
The person we seek must have the following:
A diploma or bachelor’s degree in Engineering, or related technical field, or a Business Management diploma or Degree with a technical mindset capable of handling technical issues in depot
Minimum of 5 years work experience in similar industry
Background in the analyses of fuels and lubricants would be advantage
Knowledge of Petroleum Industry Products and Facilities.
Knowledge of Engineering related to maintenance of Fuel Depot facilities
Stock and Supply Process experience
Supervisory and Team Management experience
Well-developed interpersonal, written, and oral communication skills, proficiency Accounting/ Sales and MS Office systems.
Ability to effectively Train and Mentor staff
Ability to manage multiple tasks with well-developed time management skills, an ability to prioritize the work.
Maintain a customer focus and thereby contribute to the growth of the company
Excellent communication skills
Team player and neat and tidy appearance
To Apply
Interested applicants who meet the above requirements, click on the link below and submit your application together with current updated CV, work references and certificates (1 PDF File).
https://boards.briohr.com/islandspetroleum-qcgswn72q5/details/690d274774cb3f0008940ab3

25106.description:
Engineer – Mechanical – Engineering Projects
Porgera, Enga, Papua New Guinea
Job Description
About New Porgera
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a company incorporated in Papua New Guinea and owns the Porgera Gold Mine in Enga Province. The Porgera Gold Mine will employ nearly 3,000 Papua New Guineans at full production, and over the last 30 years of life of the mine it has contributed approximately 10% of Papua New Guinea’s total annual exports
NPL is currently seeking a qualified and experienced individual to join the Capital & Projects team as an
Engineer – Mechanical – Engineering Projects – Capital Projects
.
(236773)
About the role
Reporting to the
Senior Engineer – Engineering Projects
, the successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing mechanical engineering projects, ensuring the safe, efficient, and cost-effective completion of all tasks related to mechanical systems and infrastructure within the mining operation.
In this role, you will.
Plan, design, and execute mechanical engineering projects, ensuring they meet safety, quality, and cost objectives.
Provide technical expertise in mechanical systems, including maintenance, upgrades, and new installations.
Coordinate with cross-functional teams, including contractors, other engineers and production and management teams, to ensure project timelines and goals are met.
Maintain engineering and production related documentation, such as procedures, work methods, costing and Bills of Materials.
Conduct risk assessments, monitor project progress, and report on performance against objectives.
Ensure compliance with industry standards, company policies, and relevant regulations.
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environment awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering or related field. IEPNG accreditation will be well regarded
Minimum of 5 years of experience in mechanical engineering, preferably in the mining industry.
Strong understanding of mechanical systems, project management, and engineering principles.
Proven ability to lead and manage engineering projects from inception to completion.
Excellent communication, problem-solving, and leadership skills.
Commitment to health, safety, and environmental standards.
Design experience using 3D modelling/AutoCAD
Why New Porgera
In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge. This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve plant performance and people knowledge.  You will be joining an operation that safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contribute to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.
Mobilization Requirement
This position is open to
PNG Citizens
Only
Rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off FIFO basic
Must successfully pass a pre-employment medical including drug and alcohol screening. (This will be arranged only for successful candidates who progress after the interview stage).
Must Have an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months)
Advert closing date:  20th November 2025
Apply

The Gender Equality Diversity & Social Inclusion (GEDSI) Officer is responsible to lead and implement initiatives that promote Gender Equality Diversity & Social Inclusion within the workplace and also the community that we serve. About us 


K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate. 


We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.


About the role


Provide front line leadership, support, mentoring and service in all geology activities, associated with exploration and resource drilling, core processing, sample analysis and resource evaluation.


Key / Major Accountabilities


Key accountabilities of this position include.




Manage all Exploration sampling activities – including but not limited to drilling, rock chip, soil sampling.


Surveying and mapping designated areas / prospects.


Analysing geological data using specialist computer applications.


Preparing reports, both internal and statutory, physicals and forecast. Complete all reports in a timely manner, adhering to strict deadlines.

Drill hole planning, designs and roll out.

Computer proficiency in MS Office suite and the ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.


Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.


Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.


Excellent trouble-shooting skills.


Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.




Life at K92  


Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.


We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster. 


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

25088.description:
Job Opportunity: Research Health Extension Officers (HEOs) – HEAL-PNG Project
Location:
Morobe & East New Britain Provinces, Papua New Guinea
Duration:
2-year contract (Full-time)
Employer:
Burnet Institute PNG
About the Burnet Institute
The Burnet Institute is an Australian medical research and public health organisation working to improve the health of vulnerable communities in Australia and globally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has operated for nearly two decades, partnering with provincial health authorities and local stakeholders to strengthen health systems, pilot innovations, and conduct research on priority health issues.
About the HEAL-PNG Project
HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in
Morobe
and
East New Britain
provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.
About the Role
The
Research Health Extension Officer (HEO)
will play a key role in establishing and implementing the HEAL-PNG trial across selected health facilities. Working closely with the Provincial Health Authority (PHA), facility staff, and the HEAL-PNG project team, the HEO will support study coordination, site setup, staff training, and data collection activities.
The position will require initiative, attention to detail, and the ability to build strong working relationships across multiple stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
Coordinate study activities at participating facilities, ensuring adherence to research protocols and ethical standards.
Facilitate site onboarding, including assessments and staff training in NCD, TB, and HIV management.
Manage data collection, entry, and quality assurance in a confidential and timely manner.
Maintain strong communication with facility and PHA staff, fostering collaboration and problem-solving.
Support logistics for meetings, trainings, and field activities.
Assist with procurement, stock control, and management of project materials and consumables.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential:
Health Extension Officer qualification (Diploma + 1-year residency or Bachelor’s + 2-year residency).
Strong understanding of tuberculosis, HIV, and non-communicable diseases (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, asthma, COPD).
Competency in Microsoft Office applications.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with fluency in English and Tok Pisin.
Strong organisational skills and ability to work both independently and in a team.
Ability to build rapport with health staff and community members.
Willingness to be based in Morobe or East New Britain and work in field-based settings.
Punctual, reliable, and proactive.
Desirable:
Experience in clinical research or health program implementation.
Other Requirements
Compliance with Burnet Institute’s occupational health, safety, and safeguarding standards.
Police Check and Working with Children Check (as applicable).
How to Apply
Please submit your
cover letter and current CV
outlining how your skills and experience align with the position to:
[email protected]
Subject line:
Research HEO – HEAL-PNG (Morobe or ENB)
Applications close:
19th November 2025
Apply

Finance Officer 


Position Description










Reporting to:






Provincial Coordinator






Work location:






East New Britain, Simbu










Department:






Program Operations - finance






Budget holder:






No










Grade






4






Direct reports:






No










 


Here you’ll make a difference


Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. The Child Nutrition and Social Protection Project is an 18-month project implemented from March 2025 to December 2026 in the provinces of East New Britain and Simbu.


 


Here your skills will be valued


Role Purpose


Reporting to the Provincial Coordinator, the Finance Officer ensures that all expenses, activities, and financial transactions are fully processed, acquitted, and documented in a timely, transparent, and equitable manner – and in accordance with Save the Children, government, and donor policies and requirements and in a transparent and accountable manner. The Finance Officer works with the project teams to ensure that all funds disbursed to respective provinces are fully acquitted and in line with government and donor requirements.


 


Key Areas of Accountability


Financial Control Framework




Full compliance with the Save the Children’s Pacific Australia Finance Manual and Save the Children in PNG’s Internal Delegation Document.


Mentor and support the team (including Village Health Assistants and Community Development Workers) to process all financial transactions and acquittals in line with policies and donor guidelines.


All breaches of the Save the Children Pacific Finance Manual are promptly recorded and reported.




 


Monthly Acquittals, Forecasts, and Financial Reports




Support the program team to review all financial transactions and supporting documents to deliver accurate monthly acquittals; ensure copies are kept on file.


Support the team to ensure that all documents and reports are prepared, submitted, and filed in accordance with donor requirements procedures in an orderly and timely manner; ensure copies are kept on file.


Deliver disbursement forecasts in a responsive, timely and quality manner, in accordance with donor requirements.


Address internal and external audit/document review/ donor sampling queries in a timely manner with relevant supporting documentation as relevant.




 


Financial Risk Management and Compliance




Financial Risk Assessments for projects are updated in a timely manner in collaboration with the donor.




 


 


 


Financial Literacy Training




Provide Financial Literacy Training of Trainers (ToTs) Trainings with support of the Cash Technical Advisor for Village Health Assistants and Community Development Workers, ensuring that they accurately transfer the knowledge to project participants.


Empower with Practical Budgeting Skills: Teach community workers how to guide individuals and families in creating realistic budgets, tracking expenses, and setting financial goals that align with their income and lifestyle.


Demystify Banking and Credit Systems: Provide clear, culturally relevant explanations of savings accounts, loans, interest rates, and credit scores to help communities make informed decisions and avoid predatory financial practices.


Promote Sustainable Financial Behaviours: Equip workers with tools to encourage long-term habits like saving regularly, planning for emergencies, and understanding the value of financial planning for education, health, and retirement.




 


Bank Accounts, Mibank and Petty Cash




Work with respective program team to ensure an accurate analysis and audit trail of all office bank and petty cash movements.




 


General




Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.


Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.


Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements




Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.


Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
, 
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.


Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.


Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.


Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.




 


Health, safety, security and risk management 
 




Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.

Lead sustainability and ESG initiatives in logistics operations
Collaborate with diverse teams on innovative environmental and social programs
Join an organisation that values innovation, quality and professional growth
About the Company
 A well-established PNG-based company with diverse portfolio spanning property development, logistics, retail, and hospitality. The organisation has a long-standing presence in the market and continues to expand its operations across the country. It provides a structured and supportive environment for employees to develop their careers.
 
 
About the Role
 The organisation is currently seeking 
an Environment, Social and Governance (ESG) Specialist
 to lead the development and implementation of strategies that enhance ESG performance across logistics operations. In this role, you will focus on reducing environmental impact, promoting ethical practices, ensuring compliance with regulations, and supporting social initiatives across the organisation.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
 
 
Implement programs to reduce carbon emissions, improve fuel efficiency, and promote sustainable practices across the business operations.
 
Monitor environmental metrics and explore renewable energy, low-emission technologies, and waste reduction solutions.
 
Ensure safe and ethical working conditions, align logistics practices with ESG policies, support social initiatives in education, health, and economic development, and ensure compliance with ethical standards.

Conduct ESG risk assessment, particularly related to supply chain transparency and community relations and prepare timely reports for stakeholders.
 
Collect and analyse data, track performance, identify trends and prepare sustainability reports and presentations.
 
Work closely with internal teams and external partners to understand ESG requirements, influence practices, and drive alignment with corporate sustainability goals.
 
 
Requirements of the Role
 
 
Bachelor degree in Environmental Science, Sustainability, Business, or related field.
 
Minimum 3+ years in ESG, sustainability, or corporate social responsibility, ideally in logistics, shipping, transportation, or extractive industries in PNG or the Pacific region.
 
Knowledge of ESG frameworks and sustainability reporting standards.
 
Strong analytical skills for data collection, metrics tracking and reporting.
 
Excellent communication and interpersonal skill to collaborate with diverse teams and influence stakeholders.
 
Ability to manage multiple prioritise and deliver results in in a fast-paced environment.
 
 
 
 
To apply for this position, interested candidates are asked to submit:
 
 
 
A cover letter addressing key criteria of the role
 
An updated CV in Microsoft Word format, outlining employment history, educational qualifications, and listing three referees (referees will only be contacted if shortlisted)
 
 
 
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

24926.description:
PAPUA NEW GUINEA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY


The Papua New Guinea University of Technology is located in the industrial city of Lae, the second largest city in Papua New Guinea.  The city of Lae has an airport with flights to any location in PNG. The University is the only technological university in the country.  It has a main campus and three amalgamated colleges.  The main campus has 14 academic departments including one in Open and Distance Learning (ODL).  It offers undergraduate and graduate programs in engineering, natural and applied sciences, built environment, language and business.  The university has an Information Technology Services department and a Library.


MATHESON LIBRARY


Matheson Library, named after the first Chancellor of the University, which was founded in 1967. It has a current book stock of 130,000 volumes and receives 600 periodical titles. It is the only library in the university serving some 250 academic staff and 3,000 full time students taking a range of degree, diploma and certificate courses in Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Mining, Communication Engineering, Business Studies, Architecture and Building, Surveying and Land Studies, Mathematics and Computer Sciences, Applied Sciences, Applied Physics, Forestry, Agriculture and Communication and Development Studies.


The library system is automated and it operates 7 days a week with limited operation during weekends. The library seeks to appoint a suitably qualified and highly experienced person to immediately fill the following vacancy.


UNIVERSITY LIBRARIAN


The University Librarian is responsible for the overall management and development of library services, collections, budget and staff.  The University is concerned that it gains access to the information superhighway and its new Librarian will be expected to accelerate this process.


Duties and Responsibilities:




Efficient Information Literacy and Accessibility.






Ensure that Students and Staff have access to library resources effectively and resourcefully and at the same time students and staff are well inducted on the library operations. 




    2.
    Well Maintained Accessibility Resources Center.




All electronic accessibility equipment, books and journals are readily available for staff and students. All library books and journals are acquired on time for students and staff.




 
  3. Academic Success for Students and Staff.




To maintain continuous flow of information between academic departments and students required for research and study.




 
  4.Research Impact
.




Ensuring all PNGUoT research articles and papers are well preserved




   5
.Sustain and uphold University’s wellbeing and Identity through effective Clients Service by:


    ● 
Maintaining a decent professional relationship with other libraries in the country and overseas for inter-         library loan purposes. 


 
  6.Capacity development of fellow colleagues




Continuously mentoring of library staff skills and knowledge to be able to better serve staff, students and other clients.




 
7. Actively participate in Policy development for the library.


 


Qualifications & Experience




A relevant master’s degree and an internationally recognized professional qualification in librarianship.


Required to have experience working in academic or research libraries and operational concepts involved in the delivery of users and bibliographic services and library automation.


Must be able to manage emerging trends in academic libraries especially those resulting from electronic access to information.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills, business skills and good interpersonal skills




 


Conditions of Service


Base Salary Range:
 
Professor  
 PGK 95,366 – PGK116,558 per annum


Base DMA Range:
                      PGK 43,069 – PGK 74,653 per annum


Base IMA Range:
                      PGK 105,320 – PGK162,617 per annum


 


DMA = Domestic Market Allowance


IMA = International Market Allowance


 


(Level of appointment depends upon qualification and experience)


 


Initial contract period is for three years. Benefits include a gratuity of 30% of salary in the first year, 35% in the second year and 40% in the third year (paid on a fortnightly basis), support for approved research, appointment and repatriation fares for yourself and dependents, book & equipment allowance of PGK1,000.00 per annum, settling-in/out allowance of PGK1,700.00 for single & PGK3,600.00 for accompanied plus PGK200.00 for each of two authorized dependent children (under 19 years) on appointment and repatriation, six weeks paid leave per year, recreation leave fares for yourself, spouse & two authorized dependents after 18 months of service and education fares and assistance towards school fees for authorized dependents are available. Staff members are also permitted to earn from consultancy up to 50% of earnings annually. Consultancy projects need to be approved by the respective Head of Department and the Vice Chancellor's office. Furnished accommodation is provided on campus. All earnings in PNG attract income tax, the tax rates are progressive and the maximum rate is 40%.


Application procedure


Suitable candidates are invited to send detailed application with curriculum vitae, publication list, summary of her/his educational activity, research interest, and certified copies of qualifications. They should provide names and addresses, including email addresses, fax/phone numbers of three (3) referees, at least one of whom should be a past/present employer or supervisor, should be sent to:

For more details about this position and other opportunities, visit:

25087.description:
Workplace Type: On Site
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
To safely carry out maintenance and repairs to all equipment associated with the Newmont In-pit fleet as directed by the supervisor. And ensure that all plant and equipment is maintained to Newmont's requirements and meet all safety, availability, and production target KPI’s.
To provide mechanical fitting services on mobile fleet units within an open pit environment
Specific focus is to be on Shovels & Drills.
Essential Duties
Ensure personal and team compliance with all company HSE requirements & policies including Fitness for Work.
Complete any HSE tasks only if the hazards and any potential consequences are understood and any corrections are firstly agreed by the relevant Supervisor.
Display behavior consistent with Newmont Values.
Provide ongoing daily services in inspecting, fault-finding/troubleshooting, repairing and testing mechanical equipment on mobile fleet as required.
Ensure documentation, maintenance and service records for equipment are complete and kept up to date
Actively seek cost reduction opportunities and identifies & reports any cost wastage within designated area.
Work constructively within a diverse group of people.
Deliver consistently on commitments and takes accountability for own development.
Training & Experience
3 – 5 years relevant work experience essential in heavy industry preferably within a mining environment.
Experience with the following equipment will be looked upon favorably; Hitachi 2600, O&K RH200,Cat 6020 & 6060 Dig units, Epiroc D65 drill, D55 Sandvik drills, Epiroc/Atlas Copco PV271 or 231 Pit Viper Rotary Blast Hole Drill.
Trade Certificate in Heavy Equipment Fitter or equivalent.
Relevant tertiary qualification advantageous.
PNG Driver's Licence - Class 6 essential.
Previous experience in delivery and assessment of training desirable.
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work autonomously from time to time.
High attention to detail with good time management skills.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills.
Demonstrate personal responsibility for own health and safety and develop an understanding of the legal requirement, HSE standards and standard operating procedures relevant to direct work area.
Work well with others, listen actively, seek inputs and ask clarification questions to check understanding staying focused and composed in a variety of work situations.
Effectively manage own time to complete tasks in line with job expectations and requirements adjusting plans to cater for unforeseen events / disruptions.
Recognise problems and proactively work toward resolution under the guidance of immediate Supervisor.
Recognise opportunities to minimise waste and addresse it according to the HSE and operational standards and practices.
Working Conditions
The position is in Lihir at the Mobile Fleet Maintenance Shovel Pad.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply
before closing date: 17 November 2025
– we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

Communications & External Affairs Officer
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Communications & External Affairs Officer
to join our team. permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
The Communication and External Affairs (C&EA) officer shall promote a positive public image and control the dissemination of information on the company’s behalf.
Everyone at St Barbara Limited is required to understand and act in accordance with St Barbara’s values and policies and meet all relevant internal and external compliance obligations. The role incumbent and manager will identify and review the specific compliance requirements of the role.
The Opportunity
Technical Accountabilities
Ensure a healthy and safe work environment and that work standards are maintained and enhanced
Develop and maintain effective communication strategies, channels, tools, templates, and procedures to continuously surpass expectations
Managing internal communications
Coordinate the communication of strategies, business results and messages from senior leadership
Drafting and placing content for mass media and internal company platforms/tools
Responding to media enquiries and performing media outreach to achieve brand placement in publications
Fostering relationships with advocates and key stakeholders
Organising mine visits for government officials and other stakeholders
Organising internal and external events and campaigns
Assisting the leadership team in managing communication in a crisis
Ensuring that communication material aligns with brand standards
Maintaining digital media archives including photos and videos
Monitoring media coverage on the business
Monitoring, evaluating, and creating reports detailing successes and failures of communications events and campaigns
Deliver clear messages which motivate our employees and communities to act in unison towards meeting business objectives.
Proven ability to film, record, and produce professional-quality video content tailored for corporate use and external presentations.
Skilled in graphic design for media publications and external events, with a focus on visually impactful and brand-aligned content
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Bachelor of Communication or relevant field
4 – 5 years communication experience
Proven experience as communications and external affairs officer
Proficient command of English and Tok Pisin
Excellent oral, written and presentation skills
Experience in social media platforms and content production
Well-developed knowledge in the use MS Office; photo and Video-editing and audio editing software is an asset
Experience in Mining and or Heavy Industry is an advantage
Desirable
Enthusiasm and responsibility for the role
Exhibits personal commitment
Manages time effectively and meets deadlines
Is punctual for internal and external appointments
For further information on the
Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/NATDF
Closing date: Saturday, 15 November 2025 at close of business.
Please submit your Applications, CVs, and Supporting documents (all merged in one PDF document)
At Simberi Gold Company Limited, we’re committed to finding the best fit for every role. We are a diverse and inclusive workplace, welcoming diversity in all its forms. All qualified applicants will be given equal consideration, regardless of their race, national origin, gender, age, religion, disability, sexual orientation or gender identity.
Apply
