25045.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION










TITLE 






PEOPLE, CULTURE & SAFEGUARDING COORDINATOR   










REPORTING TO






OPERATIONS MANAGER










LOCATION






PORT MORESBY 








 


 








CLASSIFICATION






D2










EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS






PERMANENT 










Introduction


WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.


 


WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is in the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.


 


WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.


Everything we do is shaped by our six values:




Integrity


Respect


Collaboration


Courage


Accountability


Innovation




 


WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.


WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.


 


WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to take action. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission. 




Position Summary


The People, Culture, and Safeguarding Coordinator plays an essential role in promoting safe and positive team culture and operations at WaterAid Papua New Guinea. Reporting to the Operations Manager, this role ensures systems and processes for people management are fit for purpose and supports staff and managers to effectively complete tasks from recruitment, through leave, growth and performance management, and staff exit. They will manage feedback and complaint mechanisms and support the Senior Management Team to make effective decisions in line with both WaterAid Federation and PNG compliance requirements regarding people & HR. As Safeguarding Lead for WaterAid Papua New Guinea, this role will manage safeguarding training and reporting processes and support all staff to meet PSEAH compliance requirements for a safer working environment for staff as well as those we work with through our projects. The People, Culture, and Safeguarding Officer connects with regional and global WaterAid colleagues for training, support, and collaboration.


 


Key Accountabilities


Systems, Processes, and Staff Engagement




Lead and maintain all people policies, manual, processes and administration in line with current legislation and WaterAid global policies (i.e. recruitment, employment contracts, casuals and consultants contracts, starters, leavers and change processes, org chart, JDs) and standards. Support Managers to deliver these with staff effectively.


Ensure all staff information with Nasfund, IRC, NCSL, Medical Insurance and Police Clearance for starters and continuing staff are update to date.


Manage processing of all work permits, NID, passports and visa for national, regional and global staff as and when required.  


Administer the internal web-based People Place HR management system, and support staff and managers to use this effectively.


Manage and continuously improve WaterAid PNG reward ensuring an appropriate mix of pay, benefits and non-pay rewards in line with WaterAid’s reward principles and national legislation. Contribute to reward benchmarking and support managers to communicate to employees about total reward. Coordinate with SMT and Global People Team.


Foster high levels of employee engagement, including staff participation in the Global Employee Engagement surveys (GEES) and line manager capability, coordinating GEES action plans. Organise Staff Days and Induction sessions.


Lead the Country Training and Development Plan and team building activities including Staff Retreats


Collate and accurately analyse people data and metrics for use within the Country Program and organisational wide people reporting requirements.


Engage with the wider Global People team and build connections to other organisations, accessing appropriate learning and resources for the WAPNG team. 




 


Provide support to the SMT and people managers to enhance our people management processes




Embed and role model a strong performance management culture and processes. Advise staff and managers in agreeing appraisal objectives, holding honest conversations, delivering feedback and recognizing success. 


Advise Operations Manager and Country Director on issues of under-performance, plan and 
implementing performance improvement plans where required.


Ensure new and transitioning employees and volunteers receive a planned, effective and timely induction and exit, and advise managers on their role in delivering this.


Work with the Operations Manager and Country Director to build Manager capability and behaviors. 


Provide specialist advice and instruction to SMT and managers on employee relations issues (i.e. disciplinary, grievance, capability, bullying and harassment) in line with CP policy, Global WaterAid policies and legislation, working with legal providers as needed. Inform Organizational Risk Assessment


Give accurate and appropriate advice, training and support to managers to recognize, respect and enable diversity and inclusion.


Advise managers to identify employee learning and career aspirations and agree on effective development plans. Recommend suitable learning methods and develop an annual Country Program learning and development plan, supported by learning initiatives from the global people team.


Support managers in identifying and maximizing potential and drive development through succession planning and individual development planning to meet our skills and capability needs.




 




Safeguarding Lead






Champion safeguarding principles through people and culture activities


Act as a Safeguarding focal point, receiving safeguarding reports and processing these in line with WaterAid Policy & processes


Revise and maintain policies, processes, and resources related to safeguarding and protection against sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEAH). 


Deliver training and information to staff, volunteers, and collaborators in line with policy and standard requirements


Manage internal and external feedback, complaints, and reporting mechanisms


Monitor completion of project risk assessments and application of nominated risk mitigation strategies, report status to Country Director




 


Qualification, Skills & Attributes (Key Capabilities/Selection Criteria) 










Essential










Experience








Minimum of three years’ work experience in a similar role 


Experience in designing or providing effective training modules 


Excellent communication skills and ability to make clear engaging presentations in English


Good networker adept at establishing and maintaining relationships with colleagues and collaborators. 


Knowledge of Papua New Guinea labour law and requirements












Knowledge and skills








Proficient with the use of Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.


Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and Tok Pisin. 


Excellent time management skills, flexibility, and an ability to prioritise tasks 












Education








Completion of a degree course in a relevant area, ideally in human resources or related field.












Personal qualities








An ability to effectively work independently and as a member of a team 


A ‘can do’ attitude 


Excellent communication and interpersonal skills


An ability to manage confidentiality and handle sensitive information


Attention to detail


A commitment to WaterAid’s values and Child safeguarding policies












Physical Environment and Demands


Ergonomic work stations within an open plan office. 


 


Level of contact with children


The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times. 


To Apply:


Please submit an application to 
[email protected]


 by 14
th
 November 2025.


Applications for this position must include a resume and a cover letter addressing the above Qualification, Skills and Selection Criteria. 


 


Applicants must have the right to work in Papua New Guinea








Apply

Location: Lae, Morobe


CCTV technician - Job Description


CCTV technician is responsible for installing and maintaining closed-circuit television systems. They commonly work with video cameras, monitors, recording devices, networking equipment, and other related hardware to ensure that these systems are functioning properly at all times.


CCTV technician may also be called upon to troubleshoot problems with the system or its components. This might involve anything from replacing broken parts to diagnosing software issues or other technical difficulties.


CCTV Technician Skills Required


Technical skills:
 Technical skills are the abilities and knowledge that allow you to perform tasks and complete projects. Technical skills are essential for a CCTV technician as they allow you to install, repair and maintain security systems. Technical skills can include knowledge of electrical systems, computer software and security protocols.


Communication skills:
 Communication skills are necessary for a CCTV technician to have, as they must be able to clearly relay information to other technicians, and managers. They must also be able to listen to and understand requests from managers.


Attention to detail:
 Attention to detail is the ability to notice small changes in a situation. It’s important for CCTV technicians to notice small changes in a room or area they’ve already inspected. This allows them to identify any new security threats and ensures they’ve thoroughly checked the area.


Problem-solving skills:
 Problem-solving skills are essential for CCTV technicians because they often encounter challenges while installing and maintaining security systems. For example, if a camera isn’t working properly, a technician might need to find the source of the problem and fix it. Similarly, if a security system malfunctions, a technician might need to troubleshoot the system and find a solution.


Ability to work independently:
 Working independently means that you can complete tasks without the help of others. As a CCTV technician, you may be required to install and repair security systems on your own. This means that you need to have the knowledge and skills necessary to complete the task.


As a CCTV technician at Express Freight Management, you will be responsible for the installation, configuration, and maintenance of our CCTV systems. You will work with our team to ensure that our systems are up-to-date and functioning properly. You may be required to do training or be required to attend training that concerns CCTV systems. You are required to have experience with CCTV systems and networking, as well as a strong understanding of security protocols. You will be required to be detail-oriented and able to work independently.


Duties & Responsibilities


CCTV Roles




Install, maintain, and troubleshoot CCTV systems according to company standards and department specifications.


Perform site surveys to assess department needs and recommend solutions.


Generate system diagrams and documentation for both internal use.


Provide technical support and advice to departments as needed.


Respond to service calls in a timely and professional manner.


Keep up to date with the latest industry developments and technologies.


Maintain and document accurate records of all installed systems.


Always adhere to health and safety guidelines.


Comply with all company policies and procedures.


Installing, maintaining, repairing, and replacing security cameras, computer networks, and other equipment used in video surveillance systems and Information Systems (IT).


Monitoring the operation of security equipment for malfunctions or other problems


Installing and maintaining security equipment such as alarms, access control, or time attendance systems


Structural network cabling and installation




Required Skills and Qualifications




High school diploma or equivalent


2+ years experience in installation, maintenance, and repair of CCTV systems


Working knowledge of CCTV equipment, including cameras, DVRs, and monitors


Ability to read and interpret technical manuals and drawings


Basic computer skills, with aptitude to learn new software and systems




Preferred Skills and Qualifications




4+ years experience in installation, maintenance, and repair of CCTV systems


Strong working knowledge of CCTV equipment, including cameras, DVRs, and monitors


Proficient in configuring CCTV systems


Experience developing and implementing CCTV systems

Looking for a Change?


Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.


EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT


 
Finance Manager – Goroka Based


CARE International in PNG is recruiting for a Finance Manager position and its based in Goroka. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.


The Finance Manager will provide effective leadership of the Finance and Grants team in CARE PNG. The FM is also responsible for all aspects of the financial and grants management, working collaboratively with Logistics and Program teams to ensure consistent compliance with the CARE Australia COFM (Country Office Finance Manual), Contracts Management Policy, CIPNG local policies, procedures and donor regulations.


The Finance Manager works under the direction of the Country Director, will lead and manage the Finance and Grant functions for the country office ensuring efficient accounting, cash management, payroll, budgeting, financial processes and donor grant reporting and acquittal.


The FM provides effective support to SMT (Senior Management Team) including timely management reports to achieve optimal management of financial resources and effective financial management risk in place.


This role will foster effective communication, coordination and collaboration within the Finance, Grants and other finance teams across the Organisation.


SELECTION CRITERIA




Minimum Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or equivalent and/ or a 7-8 years relevant work experience, in finance and grants for an International Non-Government Organisation (INGO);


Qualified Certified Practicing Accountant (CPA);


Knowledge of relevant accounting standards and PNG laws and regulations;


Demonstrated high level organisational, financial and time management skills, including the ability to plan and manage workflows; work under pressure and balance competing priorities to meet reporting deadlines in a complex working environment;


Demonstrated understanding of gender equality and a commitment to CARE’s approach and values including ethnic diversity and cultural sensitivity;


Proven understanding of working with an International Non-Government Organisation (INGO);


Representational skills including developing networks and relationships with key stakeholders;


Fluent oral and written communication skills in both Pidgin and English; and


Fully conversant with Microsoft Office 365 and financial management software, preferably SUN




 
For more information, request a copy of the full Position Description and Terms & Conditions via the below details or phone: 532 2740 or mobile 7196 8447

email:

P.O Box 1157, Goroka, 441 Eastern Highlands Province.

th

 Only short-listed applicants will be contacted.

CARE PNG is committed to safeguarding children and the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse.

25042.description:
About Newmont


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Purpose










As an Team Lead, Emergency Response, you’ll play a critical role in protecting people, property, and the environment. Your leadership and technical expertise will ensure our site is always prepared to respond effectively to emergencies—medical, fire, rescue, or hazardous materials.


As part of our team, you will












Support and execute emergency response plans tailored to site-specific risks and regulations


Maintain and inspect emergency equipment to ensure operational readiness


Lead and participate in drills, simulations, and training sessions


Deliver emergency response training to site personnel and ERT members


Act as Incident Controller or delegate during emergencies


Mentor and coach ERT members to build a high-performing, cohesive team


Contribute to investigations, audits, and continuous improvement initiatives


Represent Emergency Response in engagements with regulators, contractors, and suppliers




Prerequisites for your success in this role












Support and execute emergency response plans tailored to site-specific risks and regulations


Maintain and inspect emergency equipment to ensure operational readiness


Lead and participate in drills, simulations, and training sessions


Deliver emergency response training to site personnel and ERT members


Act as Incident Controller or delegate during emergencies


Mentor and coach ERT members to build a high-performing, cohesive team


Contribute to investigations, audits, and continuous improvement initiatives


Represent Emergency Response in engagements with regulators, contractors, and suppliers




Your work environment










You’ll be based on-site on a FIFO 28:14 roster, working within the Safety & Sustainability function. This is a hands-on role requiring 24/7 emergency preparedness, with responsibilities that span training, equipment readiness, and real-time incident response. You’ll collaborate closely with site management, operational teams, and external stakeholders including regulators and contractors.


Why Join Newmont


At Newmont, safety is more than a priority—it’s a core value. You’ll be part of a global team committed to responsible mining, innovation, and continuous improvement. We invest in your growth, support your well-being, and empower you to make a meaningful difference every day.










At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 13 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!


 








Apply

25037.description:
We are seeking to recruit a 
Senior Expeditor
 for our 
Commercial – Procurement Department
 in Lae. Reporting to the 
Purchasing Supervisor (Lae)
. The
 Senior Expeditor
 will be in charge of coordination, execution and ensuring that procured goods are received on site prior to the required date and to ensure that critical supplier DIFOT (Delivery-in-Full-On-Time) performance remains at an acceptable level.


Key roles and responsibilities include:


• To ensure all purchased stock items are delivered to the supplier on or before the nominated delivery date and to ensure that any defaults on delivery are immediately referred to the respective end -user, the Warehouse & Logistics Superintendent and the Purchasing Supervisor.
• To report in full to the Supply Superintendent, the Warehouse & Logistics Superintendent, the Purchasing Supervisor and relevant customers on a regular basis and pro -actively advise them of any delivery risks or delays that may have a significant impact on delivery schedules and stock item availability.
• To support Logistics with setting priorities for the contracted freight forwarders.
• Key supplier DIFOT performance management and reporting.
• Update and maintain the relevant status information or databases, including Pronto, with current status of all stock PO’s.
• In collaboration with Purchasing, Inventory, Logistics and End-users support the confirmation of specific PO freight mode and nomination of vessel to freight forwarders to achieve scheduled arrival targets.
• Prioritize expediting activities to ensure emphasis on all time critical PO’s.
• Work with end-users to understand and comprehend their specific demand requirements and take action accordingly.
• Collaborate with Purchasing to ensure that delivery details in PO’s are updated to reflect latest confirmed delivery status.
• Engage with suppliers to verify progress of the PO and reports back on status.
• Maintains expediting reports and feedback with all team members.
• Ensure details and accurate reporting of relevant information on time.
• Provide support as required to the Purchasing Supervisor.
• Read, understand and follow policy and procedures.
• Coach customer departments on how they can contribute to increased availability.


Qualifications, Skills and Experience required:


• Tertiary qualification in Supply Chain or Logistics Management.
• Grade 10 & 12 Certificates
• Minimum of 5 years’ expediting, logistics or purchasing experience.
• Sound knowledge in Pronto (or similar ERP) and the full suite of Microsoft products in particular Excel.
• Prior PNG mining industry experience in disciplines such as inventory and/or warehousing
• Excellent interpersonal relationship and conflict management, teamwork and communication skills.
• Understanding of Incoterms.
• Strong written and verbal skills.
• Remote location or operating environment experience
• Understanding of purchasing, logistics, production planning and inventory management.
• Broad knowledge of both domestic and international freight forwards and shipping agents and the tracking systems they deploy.


The above role is Lae based.


If you are interested in this exciting and challenging opportunity and confident you have the skills, knowledge and experience to full-fill this role, then please apply by email to;
[email protected]

 Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.


Application closes on Thursday 13th November, 2025

25033.description:
About Newmont


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact. 










Purpose






Efficiently manage dispatch operations by implementing and monitoring systems, providing 
performance metrics, supporting staff training, ensuring compliance, and resolving issues to maintain 
smooth resource flow and operational accuracy










Essential Duties








Administer efficient dispatch of resources for operational needs


Monitor and supervise dispatch activities to meet operational demands


Provide on dispatch performance and metrics to the guide


Support dispatch staff in operational procedures and safety standards


Execute improvements in dispatch systems for enhanced efficiency


Supervise the maintenance of dispatch equipment and systems


Adhere to compliance with dispatch regulations and protocols


Liaise with logistics teams to ensure smooth flow of resources


Execute audits of dispatch processes to ensure accuracy


Solve any issues related to dispatch operations or resource delays


Explain the purpose of the work of your team and how it adds value to the business.


Encourage your team members to identify critical issues which will affect the work.


Listen when issues are raised.


Allocate work to your team members from the plan set by the manager.


Review how team members are performing with their work.


Recognise team members for work done well.


Actively contributes to establishing and maintaining a positive and productive team working environment












Training & Experience








Relevant academic qualification or trade qualification


Practical knowledge gained from working in relevant mining role - applied knowledge of technical aspects of the role including processes, equipment and systems.


Practical and applied knowledge of working safely and sustainably in this area of mining


Proven ability to identify risk and taking active steps to mitigate risk


Acquired knowledge of business and process improvement-identifying improvement opportunity and taking 
appropriate action


For supervisor roles, applied knowledge of managing, leading and supervising mining teams


Competent in operational processes and systems required of the role


Competent in safety, health, and sustainability processes and procedures


Foundational understanding of the processes of parallel areas of work - for example planning, drill and blast, maintenance, processing. 


Competent to deliver specific activities identified in the role, and using relevant equipment


Competent in risk management and mitigation


For supervisor roles, competent in all aspects of teams management and operational performance monitoring, and in managing conflict between stakeholders












Working Conditions






Must be open to a FIFO position.
Ability to complete a pre-employment medical assessment.
Must have proof of a completed Police Clearance within the last six months.










At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply 
before 13th Oct
 – we’d love to hear from you!

24478.description:
Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About Us
K92 Mining Limited is the owner of the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth while contributing significantly to Papua New Guinea’s economy. More than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG, and our local initiatives — including educational scholarships, agricultural support, and health outreach programs — help improve quality of life and build long-term capacity in surrounding communities.


About the Role
The Superintendent – GIS & Database plays a critical role in leading K92’s spatial data management, community asset mapping, and stakeholder information systems. This role ensures the accuracy, security, and accessibility of all social performance data to support evidence-based decision-making across the mine life cycle.


Key Accountabilities
This position is responsible for managing spatial and non-spatial data systems, maintaining standards, and ensuring compliance with social performance commitments. Responsibilities include:




Leadership & Team Oversight
 – Supervise the GIS & Database team, mentor staff, and ensure quality outputs are delivered on time and within standards.


Systems & Standards Management
 – Maintain GIS and database workflows, templates, and registers in line with the Spatial Data & Community Asset Management Standard.


Data Integrity & Compliance
 – Safeguard accuracy, completeness, and security of all social performance data, ensuring readiness for audit and IFC compliance.


Collaboration & Integration
 – Work closely with Community Affairs, Exploration, Environmental, and Mine Planning teams to align data and support operational needs.


Stakeholder & Commitment Support
 – Provide mapping and database support for landowner verification, compensation agreements, and external reporting.




About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring strong technical expertise and experience in GIS and database management, ideally within mining or related industries. You will also demonstrate:




Degree in GIS, Geomatics, Geography, Information Systems, or a related field.


Sound experience in GIS and data management within mining, oil & gas, infrastructure, or environmental sectors.


Advanced knowledge of ArcGIS, QGIS, and database management systems, with strong skills in data integration and analysis.


Experience with customary land tenure systems and community mapping in PNG or similar contexts.


Strong analytical, problem-solving, and data visualisation skills, with attention to accuracy and detail.


Ability to translate complex technical concepts into accessible information for non-technical stakeholders.




 


Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, ensuring that every employee can reach their highest potential without discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides healthy meals made from locally sourced produce, along with internet, cable TV, and a gymnasium. We offer competitive salaries, performance-based incentive plans, savings programs, medical assistance, and access to wellbeing and employee assistance programs, all supported by a friendly roster system.


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP






Apply

Company :


Hastings Deering (PNG) Limited


About Us:


Hastings Deering (PNG) Limited is one of the largest Caterpillar dealer networks in the world. We sell, service and support the complete range of Caterpillar machinery used in the mining, construction, agricultural, materials handling and government sectors.  Over the last 75 years, we have built a reputation for hiring and developing the industry’s best and delivering an exemplary level of service to our customers and colleagues.


We currently have an excellent opportunity for 
8x Hose Shop Technicians 
to join our Part’s Department team based in Porgera.


About the Role:


These roles primarily exist to develop the Hydraulic Hose business to ensure Hastings Deering (PNG) Limited are in the best position to offer our customers the best market options in hydraulic hose support, sales repairs, and installations. Develop best in Class (safety & profitable) in House Hydraulic Hose Manufacturing.             


Reporting to the Parts Manager, Lae Business Centre, your competency, and experience will include:




Ensure safety goals are achieved through personal commitment, no harm to self or others and participation in safety initiatives.


Ensure business direction, team purpose, and change agenda is understood, agreed to and work activities are aligned.


Visual leadership in relation to safety, safety related metrics, solutions, and outcomes through the end-to-end supply chain.


Responsible for the effective development of the company’s Hydraulic Hose Business activities to ensure we meet our customers’ expectations.


Ensure all Hose Shop/trucks comply with all company policies, procedures including safety rules and regulations, fatigue management guidelines and chain of responsibility.


Align business technologies with industry standards to achieve integrated operations performance reporting.


Working in this fast-paced environment you will be required to use your initiative and ensure that you keep internal and external stakeholders informed of all alterations to the Hydraulic Hose Business Oversee/manage as part of the supply chain network team, annual stock takes which are to be conducted on the hose vans and the hose shop in a timely cost effective and without disruption to the customer.


Standardize Hydraulic Hose Manufacturing process across all HD hose production sites, to increase performance and profitability, and improve Customer experience.




About You:


You will bring the following skills and experience to the role:




Must have Grade 12 school certificate.


Trade qualifications in a technical field.


Experience in Hose Shop Manufacturing or Repair


Use of Hose Assembly Tools and Equipment


Excellent computer knowledge, working with Microsoft Office, Systems exposure to Microsoft Dynamics AX or similar.


Able to interpret and demonstrate knowledge in using CAT SIS 2.0 and HIS          




To express interest for these challenging and rewarding role, submit your updated CV, copies of certificates, references, and police clearance certificate through Workday.


To Apply: Click on the “Apply” button.  


Enquiries: Please call our HR Team on (675) 300 8300


Only Shortlisted candidates will be contacted.


Applications close Wednesday 12th November 2025






Apply

25017.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.


We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.


At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.


Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas suppliers, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.


For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.


 


What you’ll do:
Based in the Santos Port Moresby office, the Regional Fleet Coordinator will lead the coordination of fleet and workshop operations across the country. Your role will drive cost efficiency, safety, and operational reliability, ensuring all vehicle activities align with Santos’ Land Transport Procedure and PNG regulations.


Key Responsibilities:


Fleet Operations Management:
Lead all aspects of fleet operations, including pool vehicle oversight, workshop coordination, and cost allocation. Forecast operating costs, monitor vehicle utilisation, and ensure compliance with local transport laws, safety, mass and load limits.
Cost and Efficiency Initiatives:
Identify and deliver cost-saving measures, implement cost control systems, track compliance, and optimise asset utilisation to improve transparency and reduce financial leakage.
Team and Stakeholder Coordination:
Lead workshop maintenance teams and mechanics to minimise vehicle downtime and improve reliability. Act as the first point of contact for PNG-based staff, providing expert advice on fleet assets, land transport standards and best practice.
Training and awareness:
Develop and deliver targeted training programs on fleet operations and compliance, supporting the uplift of local capability and adherence to Santos standards.
Compliance and Technical Oversight:
Conduct regular fleet inspections, support incident investigations, and provide technical advice for decisions on vehicle grounding. Collaborate with internal teams to identify and address non-compliance, ensuring corrective actions are implemented effectively.
Governance and Safety:
Ensure full compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and corporate governance and safety requirements.


 


What you’ll bring:
Your strong technical knowledge of mechanical systems for both light and heavy vehicles, with the capability to conduct mechanical inspections and prepare detailed reports following vehicle related incidents are key. Experience working with SAP and reporting tools will further support your success in this role along with:




Good working knowledge of Papua New Guinea (PNG) regulatory and vehicle registration requirements for light and heavy vehicles.


Practical experience in workshop parts management and supply chain processes.


Proven track record in vehicle workshop or fleet management operations.


Ability to deliver coordinated operational solutions across multiple remote locations.


Strong skills in process improvement, including process mapping, cost control, and data analytics.


Excellent communication and problem-solving skills to maintain smooth fleet operations.


Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, for data analysis, reporting, and compliance tracking.


Trade qualification in Motor Mechanics or a related discipline would be highly regarded




 


What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.


At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.


Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.


 


What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.


 


How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before 
COB 12 November 2025.


A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.


 


Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is 
https://recruitment.santos.com/








Apply

Position Description


 










Reporting to:






Deputy Team Leader - Operations






Work location:






East New Britain

Program Operations

Grade






5

Here you’ll make a difference


Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organization, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. The Child Nutrition and Social Protection Project is an 18-month project implemented from March 2025 to December 2026 in the provinces of East New Britain and Simbu.


 


Here your skills will be valued


Role Purpose


Reporting to the Deputy Team Leader – Operations, the Provincial Coordinator will lead the implementation of all activities in his/her assigned province. This role will focus on coordinating and overseeing all project activities at the provincial level, ensuring effective implementation, stakeholder engagement, and alignment with Save the Children and Government of PNG national objectives.


 


Key Areas of Accountability


Program Management and Delivery




Oversee the implementation of activities in the assigned province, including project participant registration, sensitization, and trainings.


Manage the recruitment, training, and supervision of Community Development Workers (CDW) in coordination with district teams and People & Culture.


Coordinate with District Officers and CDWs to ensure timely and quality implementation of project activities.


Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for activity delivery; address any bottlenecks at the provincial level. Develop/refine provincial implementation plans, ensuring alignment with national roll-out strategies.


Support the MEAL team in any post-distribution monitoring (PDM) activities in the province


Contribute to the analysis of project data and the development of recommendations for improving project performance at the provincial level


Ensure adherence to project timelines, budgets, and donor requirements for the province. Ensure timely and accurate reporting on project activities, including financial and narrative reports




 


Operational Management




Oversee the establishment and management of offices in the province. Manage day-to-day operations at the provincial level, including logistics, procurement, and administrative functions.


Coordinate with the Deputy Team Leader and national office to ensure alignment of operational processes and systems (e.g., supply chain, human resources, finance).


Ensure compliance with Save the Children's policies, procedures, and donor requirements.




 


Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination




Serve as the primary liaison with provincial government officials, Payment Service Providers (PSPs), and other key stakeholders to facilitate smooth project implementation.


Represent Save the Children in relevant coordination meetings and forums at the provincial level. Maintain strategic relationships with provincial-level stakeholders and partners.


Coordinate closely with government/counterpart provincial coordinators.




 


Capacity Building and Support




Identify capacity-building needs for provincial and district-level staff and coordinate training opportunities. Provide mentoring and support to District Officers and CDWs.


Facilitate knowledge sharing and best practices across districts within the province.




 


General




Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.


Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.


Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.




 


Child protection and safeguarding requirements




Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.


Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s 
Child Safeguarding Policy
, 
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.


Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behavior towards children in private and professional life.


Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.


Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.


Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.




 


Health, safety, security and risk management 
 




Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.


Act safely at all times.


Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.


Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.


Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.




 


 


 


 


All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.


At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.


 


Person Specification


It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:


Mandatory Qualifications and Accreditations




Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (e.g., Development Studies, Public Health, Social Sciences). Master’s degree is an advantage.


Minimum of five (5) years of experience in project management, preferably in social protection or nutrition programs.


Strong understanding of cash transfer programs and their implementation in developing contexts


Excellent leadership and team management skills.


Proven ability to work effectively with government stakeholders and diverse partners.


Proven ability to work effectively in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Ability to think strategically, prioritize, problem-solve, and meet deadlines in a complex and challenging environment; must be culturally sensitive.


Excellent coordination and interpersonal skills with the ability to communicate and negotiate clearly and effectively at all levels and with a range of stakeholders (e.g., communities, government, donors). Proven external coordination and representation skills at a senior level.


Exhibit a strong work ethic with a high degree of flexibility with respect to working hours; ability to effectively plan and manage own time under pressure.


Excellent writing and verbal skills in English for reports and communications documents. Ability to present complex information in a succinct and compelling manner. Proficiency in Tok Pisin.


Familiarity with the local context and culture of the assigned province.




 


Additional Information 




Any offer of employment at Save the Children Australia will be subject to a satisfactory National Police Record Check and a Working with Children Check


Employees must sign on to Save the Children Australia’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.


Ongoing performance and employment will be measured against Key Performance Indicators, values, and demonstrated behaviors outlined above.


Save the Children in PNG is an Equal Opportunity Employer.




 










Driver’s Licence:






Not Required






Travel:






Frequent travel within the province










Working with Children Check:






Required






Assets:






Laptop

Job Type:
 
Permanent
 
About Us
K92 Mining Limited is the owner of the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth while contributing significantly to Papua New Guinea’s economy. More than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG, and our local initiatives — including educational scholarships, agricultural support, and health outreach programs — help improve the quality of life and build long-term capacity in surrounding communities.


About the Role
The Superintendent – Agriculture Projects is responsible for designing, implementing, and monitoring agricultural and agribusiness initiatives that enhance food security, diversify livelihoods, and create sustainable economic opportunities for local communities. These programs are a core part of K92’s social performance strategy and commitments under the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA), ensuring long-term benefits for host communities.


Key Accountabilities
This position manages the Agricultural Development Programs Standard within the Social Performance Management System (SPMS) and oversees the material issue of Strategic Community Investment – Sustainable Livelihoods & Food Security. Responsibilities include:






Leadership & Program Oversight
 – Supervise Agriculture Project Supervisors, set priorities, build capacity, and develop annual agriculture plans and budgets.






Program Delivery & Standards
 – Oversee training programs, input distribution, irrigation and infrastructure development, and market access initiatives in line with the Agricultural Development Programs Standard.






Sustainable Livelihoods & Food Security
 – Design and monitor programs that demonstrate measurable gains in productivity, income, and household food security, with a focus on climate resilience and sustainability.






Collaboration & Partnerships
 – Work with government agencies, NGOs, research institutions, and local businesses to strengthen agricultural practices and value chains.






Commitment & Expectation Management
 – Deliver MOA agricultural commitments, manage community expectations, and safeguard the company’s social licence to operate.






About You
To succeed in this role, you will have proven experience in agricultural project delivery within rural or community-based environments. You will also bring:






Degree in Agriculture, Agribusiness, or a related discipline.






Sound experience in agricultural project design and management, ideally in PNG or similar rural contexts.






Strong technical knowledge of crop and livestock production, agribusiness, and sustainable farming systems.






Demonstrated leadership skills with experience managing teams and delivering results in culturally diverse environments.






Culturally sensitive and respectful of traditional land use practices.






Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, ensuring that every employee can reach their highest potential without discrimination.


Our camp is well managed and provides healthy meals made from locally sourced produce, along with internet, cable TV, and a gymnasium. We offer competitive salaries, performance-based incentive plans, savings programs, medical assistance, and access to wellbeing and employee assistance programs, all supported by a friendly roster system.


If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.


THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

25005.description:
About Newmont


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


 


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
 










Your Impact






As an Advisor Contracts, you will play a key role in ensuring Newmont’s regional contracts for our Papua New Guinea operations are effectively managed, compliant, and aligned with our global procurement strategies. Your expertise will help secure critical goods and services, mitigate risks, and strengthen supplier and stakeholder relationships, all while supporting our commitment to safe, sustainable, and responsible mining.


 










As part of our team, you will








Deliver the procurement plan to schedule, ensuring projects stay on track and within budget.


Work closely with site stakeholders to coordinate activities, mitigate scope creep, and maintain alignment with organizational objectives.


Administer the full lifecycle of contracts, assisting the Team Lead - Category Management in implementing category strategies and ensuring appropriate contracts are in place for sourcing materials and services.


Collaborate with site operational teams to ensure contracts meet strategic objectives and support operational success.


Implement Newmont’s strategic sourcing strategies for goods and services in line with the Strategic Sourcing Playbook.


Maintain strong working relationships with internal partners and key clients, providing visibility of the supply chain vision and ensuring internal stakeholder satisfaction.


Build and sustain strong supplier relationships, ensuring open communication, timely resolution of contract-related issues, and favourable negotiation of contract changes.


Supervise all contracts and procurement activities within the sub-category to ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and company policies, including health, safety, and environmental standards.


Assess and manage risks associated with contracts, including potential legal liabilities and performance issues.
Provide regular updates on contract status, performance, and compliance, contributing insights to support the development of regional procurement methodologies.




 










Prerequisites for your success in this role








Tertiary qualification in a relevant field, such as engineering, law, business, finance, or supply chain.


Proven experience in contract management, procurement, or sourcing in mining, oil & gas, energy, or engineering industries.


Experience in end-to-end sourcing activities and contract management for direct and indirect services is essential.


Practical exposure to mining operations in PNG, including familiarity with regulatory requirements for import/export, mobilisation, and the handling of goods.


Strong knowledge of legal principles, compliance requirements, and procurement best practices.


Proficiency in SAP, Ariba, or similar ERP/eProcurement systems.


Skilled in negotiations, supplier management, and contract performance evaluation.


Strong technical skills in strategic sourcing, supplier relationship management, contracts administration, negotiations, risk identification, and dispute resolution.


Demonstrated ability to analyse data, monitor KPIs, conduct audits or reviews, and make data-driven decisions while maintaining accuracy and compliance across multiple contracts.


Excellent interpersonal, stakeholder engagement, and communication skills, with the ability to influence, collaborate, and foster strong relationships internally and externally.




 








Your work environment




Our Brisbane-based team enjoy flexible Monday to Friday work options to balance working from home and in the office. Our modern Fortitude Valley office is conveniently located near public transport and local cafés. Occasional travel to site operations and other interstate Newmont hubs may be required to support the broader team.


This is an exciting opportunity to contribute within Newmont’s Sustainability and Development function, supporting contract management activities that directly impact operational success. You’ll collaborate with diverse teams and external partners while working in a dynamic, fast-paced environment where safety, compliance, and sustainable practices are core values.


 










Why Join Newmont






At Newmont, you’ll be part of the world’s leading gold company, dedicated to creating value and improving lives through responsible mining. We offer:




A global network of operations and career growth opportunities.


A values-driven culture that prioritises safety, inclusion, and sustainability.


Competitive compensation, benefits, and professional development programs.


The chance to make a meaningful impact on both local communities and global industry standards.




 










At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.


We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!


Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 
40465
 before the advertised closing date: 
11 November 2025
.








Apply

Location: Port Moresby (POM)
Employment Type: Full-Time
Position Summary
The Facilities Maintenance Manager is responsible for the overall strategic and operational management of all company infrastructure, buildings  and grounds across the PNG network. The core function of this role is to ensure operational continuity, regulatory compliance (PNG building codes, safety laws), and the physical safety and security of all assets and personnel in a demanding environment. This requires proactive planning, robust contractor management, and strong leadership of the local maintenance team.
Key Responsibilities and Duties
Safety and Compliance (Mandatory PNG Focus)
Pioneer and enforce robust Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) standards
within the maintenance team, ensuring full compliance with the PNG Employment Act and relevant OHS regulations.
Oversee all site-specific security systems and infrastructure
(fencing, gates, lighting, surveillance) to protect high-value logistics assets from external threats.
Ensure meticulous
record-keeping and documentation
of all maintenance and safety checks for audit purposes (internal and external/ISO).
Infrastructure Management and Resilience
Develop and execute preventative maintenance (PM) programs
for all core facility systems, including complex industrial electrical systems, generators, water storage, and plumbing, addressing the risks associated with unreliable public utility services.
Oversee the
structural integrity
and repair of warehouse roofing, concrete slabs, specialized loading docks, and yard surfaces, which are frequently stressed by heavy logistics traffic and tropical weather conditions.
Manage waste stream collection, storage, and disposal (including general, recycling, and potentially on-site incinerator operation) in compliance with PNG environmental guidelines.
Respond effectively and rapidly to
critical, unscheduled facility failures
(e.g., power outages, security breaches, major equipment breakdowns) to minimize disruption to logistics operations.
Team Leadership and Local Content
Lead, mentor, and manage
the local team of tradespeople focusing on skills transfer and capacity building.
Manage service contracts and relationships with local PNG vendors and contractors
, ensuring compliance with all company and safety requirements while supporting local business development.
Oversee labor scheduling, work allocation, and performance management for the maintenance staff.
Financial and Administrative
Provide accurate and timely reporting on facility condition, maintenance KPIs, and capital needs to the General Manager.
Qualifications and Experience
Essential Requirements
Minimum of
7 years of technical experience
in industrial maintenance, facilities engineering, or a related field.
3+ years of management experience
leading maintenance teams, ideally within an industrial, mining, or logistics environment.
Strong knowledge of
PNG OHS and environmental regulations
.
Education and Certification
Technical Trade Qualification in Facilities Management.

25062.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
 
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America. 
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans. 
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way. 
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project. 
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.


What you’ll do:
Santos Foundation is seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented
 Contracts Administration Officer (CAO)
 to support our Field Operations, Support Functions, and Program teams. Based in Port Moresby this role is critical in ensuring efficient contract management and administrative support across all Foundation activities.


Key Responsibilities: 




Maintain and update the contracts tracker, ensuring timely contract renewals and closeouts.


Provide weekly status reports of contract to the Contracts Lead and Corporate Services Senior Manager.


Monitor contract compliance and escalate issues as needed.


Ensure transparency and maintain a clear audit trail for all contract activities.


Support effective communication and relationships with Santos Foundation partners.


Collaborate with Program Managers on contract-related matters.


Assist with procurement processes including purchase requisitions and receipting.


Perform general administrative duties as directed.


Ensure compliance with Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and Corporate Governance and Safety standards.




What you’ll bring:




Previous experience in an administrative role, preferably in a commercial or similar environment.


Strong time management and organizational skills.


Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Visio, Access).


Excellent written and verbal communication skills.


Ability to work independently and as part of a team.


High level of professionalism and work ethic.


Willingness to learn and adapt to new systems and processes.




Ideally, you will be a Degree or Diploma holder in Business Management, Administration, or a related field or demonstrate significant training and experience within directly relevant role(s), within large corporate environments.


What you’ll get:
 
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.


At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.


Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.


What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
 17th November 2025
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.


Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is 
https://recruitment.santos.com/






Apply

We are seeking to recruit an
 Investigator
 for our 
SHSR – Investigations Department
. Reporting to the Senior Investigator, the primary responsibility of the role is to assist with developing, implementing and maintaining the investigation systems and associated programs in PNG and to assist in the co-operation of investigation and security functions of the Hidden Valley Mining Operation.


Key roles and responsibilities include:


• Develop, secure and package physical evidence for use in legal proceedings.
• Prepare detailed reports on the observations and activities at a scene for the use in legal proceedings.
• Testify in court regarding the findings and processing methods used at the scene.
• Develop relationships with informants in order to obtain information related to cases.
• Examine records in order to locate links in chains of evidence or information.

• Collaborate with other offices and agencies in order to exchange information and coordinate activities.
• Monitor security programs designed to protect personnel, facilities, and information.

• Tertiary qualification in a related field.
• Prior police or mining investigations experience.
• Possess valid PNG’s class 6 driver’s licence.
• Be knowledgeable in aspects of incident control, search procedures, arrest & detention etc.
• Able to write concise reports & statements.
• Must be detailed oriented with strong analytical & problem-solving skills.
• Strong communications skills both written & oral, in English & Tok Pisin.
• High level computer skills in MS Word & Excel.
• Able to plan out work & meet competing deadlines.


The above role is Hidden Valley mine site based.

24988.description:
About Newmont


At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.


About Lihir


Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.


We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.


Your Impact










As a Technician, Processing, you’ll play a key role in operating critical sections of the process plant, including grinding circuits, flotation, and thickener operations. Your work ensures safety, efficiency, and production targets are met shift by shift, contributing directly to Newmont’s operational success.


As Part of Our Team, You Will










Prioritize Safety
: Ensure compliance with all HSE policies, report hazards, and actively monitor plant conditions.


Collaborate Effectively
: Work constructively with diverse teams and participate in shift handovers, toolbox meetings, and training.


Drive Production
: Operate plant equipment, complete inspections, and maintain housekeeping standards.


Control Costs
: Identify and report cost-saving opportunities and minimize waste.




Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role










Proven experience in heavy industry, preferably mining (essential).


Grade 10 education minimum.


Tertiary qualifications and metalliferous processing certificates are highly regarded.


Class 6 PNG Driver’s License.


Strong communication, attention to detail, time management, and technical knowledge in mineral processing.


Safety-conscious, proactive problem solver, team player, and adaptable to changing work conditions.




Your Work Environment












28:14 FIFO roster with flexibility for extended hours and higher duties.


Fast-paced, safety-focused mining operation on Lihir Island.


Collaborative and diverse team culture.




Why Join Newmont




Be part of a global leader in mining committed to safety, sustainability, and innovation.


Grow your career through training and development opportunities.


Work in a supportive environment that values your contribution and well-being.




At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.










We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 10 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

25031.description:
PROCUREMENT CLERK – FARM BASED 


Zenag Chicken is a nationally owned company specialised in the production, distribution, and marketing of the highest quality of farm fresh eggs and poultry products in PNG. We have served in this industry for more than 75 years. 


We are now seeking to recruit an ideal candidate for a Procurement Clerk who will be responsible for all procurement activities at our farm site. 


 
Key Responsibilities: 




Ensuring the appropriate process of raising Purchase Order is observed. 


Ensuring Purchase Orders are sent to overseas suppliers on time. 


Ensuring timely stock availability and preventing operational disruption. 


Monitoring the accuracy of the Purchase Orders to ensure no discrepancies.


Maintaining purchasing records in the system.   




 
Required Skills & Specifications 




Must have a Certificate/Diploma in Business Admin/Management. 


Certification of any procurement, supply chain or business admin course is a plus. 


Familiar with Microsoft Office, Excel & Outlook. 


Have 1 – 2 years’ experience in inventory, warehouse, or stock management systems. 


Must be flexible with working hours. 


Ability to work with minimum supervision. 


Must have good communication skills. 




 If you are interested, apply now with your updated CV, latest references and a one-page letter selling yourself to 
[email protected]
 
with the Heading Application for Inventory Clerk. Hand delivered applications can be dropped at our main office at Marsina Street, Towards Lae Main Wharf area. 


 


Please note, ONLY short-listed candidates will be contacted for an interview. 


Closing date for submissions is 08/11/2025.

25003.description:
Tabubil Engineering Limited is a major contractor to Ok Tedi Mining Ltd in Western Province of Papua New Guinea.  The company now has an immediate vacancy for a suitably qualified person for:


DRAFTSMAN DETAILER


Reporting to the Engineering & Technical Services Manager, you will be responsible for producing accurate and detailed technical drawings and models using CAD software in accordance with compliance standards. You will collaborate closely with project teams, incorporate feedback to refine designs, and communicate effectively across multicultural teams while addressing technical challenges essential to project success.


The successful applicant must possess the following attributes:




Diploma or associate degree in Drafting, CAD Design or related field


5 years’ experience in fabrication drawing; single-parts detailed drawings and assembly drawings


Proficiency in CAD Software


Strong technical drawing and design skills


Excellent attention to detail and problem-solving skills


Excellent communication and teamwork skills


Experience working in diverse and multicultural environment


Possess Class 1-6 driver’s license


Must have proof of valid medical & police clearance certificate




 


Terms and conditions to be discussed with selected candidates during interview. Single status accommodation & messing will be provided on site.
